ordered_diagnoses: Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome (Gorlin Syndrome)

facts.raw_span: multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored asymptomatic papules located on the face and vulva
The lesions first appeared around 50 years of age and gradually increased to approximately 60 lesions
Medical history was significant for a meningioma
Family history was notable for a daughter with similar facial papules that had not undergone biopsy
No palmar or plantar pits were observed
buds and cords of basaloid cells enclosing small cystic spaces
Clefting between tumor aggregates and the surrounding stroma was focally evident
Radiographic studies did not reveal any jaw cysts
A conserved splice-site mutation in SUFU gene (c.757-2A>G) in all tumor and normal tissue samples
Additional distinct deletions of the trans SUFU allele in all tumor samples
No deletions present in the normal sample

families.label: Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome (Gorlin Syndrome)

concepts.preferred_label: Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome (Gorlin Syndrome)
concepts.why: The patient's presentation of multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored papules, family history of similar lesions, and medical history of meningioma, along with the genetic findings of a SUFU gene mutation, are consistent with Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome (Gorlin Syndrome).

The histopathological features of buds and cords of basaloid cells enclosing small cystic spaces, along with clefting between tumor aggregates and the surrounding stroma, are characteristic of infundibulocystic basal cell carcinoma.
The presence of a conserved splice-site mutation in the SUFU gene and additional distinct deletions of the trans SUFU allele in all tumor samples suggests a SUFU-related basal cell carcinoma.
The family history of similar facial papules and the presence of a genetic mutation in the SUFU gene suggest a familial basal cell carcinoma.
The patient's medical history of meningioma and the presence of basal cell carcinomas suggest a possible association between the two conditions.

concepts.preferred_label: Genetic Predisposition to Basal Cell Carcinoma
concepts.why: The presence of a genetic mutation in the SUFU gene and the family history of similar lesions suggest a genetic predisposition to basal cell carcinoma.

concepts.preferred_label: SUFU-related multiple keratocystic basal cell carcinomas
concepts.why: The presence of a conserved splice-site mutation in the SUFU gene and additional distinct deletions of the trans SUFU allele in all tumor samples, with no deletions in the normal sample, explains the uncovered fact of genetic alterations in the SUFU gene.

rationales.F03: Meningioma is associated with Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome and Basal Cell Carcinoma with Meningioma.
rationales.F04: Family history of similar facial papules suggests a genetic predisposition, which is consistent with Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome, Familial Basal Cell Carcinoma, and SUFU-related basal cell carcinomas.
rationales.F06: Histopathological features of buds and cords of basaloid cells enclosing small cystic spaces are characteristic of basal cell carcinomas.
rationales.F09: A conserved splice-site mutation in the SUFU gene is a strong indicator of SUFU-related basal cell carcinomas and Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome.
rationales.F10: Additional distinct deletions of the trans SUFU allele in all tumor samples support the diagnosis of SUFU-related basal cell carcinomas and Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome.
